title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
content: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) finds relevant passages in an external collection and supplies them as context to a language model. The model can then ground its answer in those passages instead of relying only on its training data.

title: Document Chunking
content: Long documents are split into smaller chunks before embedding. A small overlap between adjacent chunks can preserve context that would otherwise fall at a chunk boundary. Chunk size and overlap should be chosen for the document and retrieval task.

title: Vector Similarity Search
content: An embedding maps text to a vector. A vector store can compare a question vector with stored document vectors and return nearby matches. Similarity search helps select context, but the retrieved passages still need to support the final answer.
